Read the events of canonical sequence data as a table

Source: R/lsa-data.R
as.data.frame.lsa_data.Rd

as.data.frame() returns the canonical sequence data from lsa_data(), every event with its sequence and position, as a tidy table, which shows how the input was read: which rows became sequences, where missing values were dropped, and which labels were assigned. For input given as a transition-count matrix, it returns one row per cell instead. print() shows the input source, the number of states, sequences, events and lag-1 transitions.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lsa_data'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_data'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An lsa_data object from lsa_data().

row.names, optional, ...

Ignored; present for consistency with the generic.

Value

as.data.frame(): a data.frame with one row per event and the columns seq_id, index (position within the sequence) and state; or, for transition-matrix input, one row per cell and the columns from, to and count. print() returns x invisibly.

See also

lsa_data(), lsa_transitions()

Examples

d <- lsa_data(list(c("a", "b", NA, "a"), c("b", "c")))
d
#> <lsa_data>
#>   source:        events
#>   states (K):    3
#>   labels:        a, b, c
#>   sequences:     2
#>   events:        5
#>   transitions:   3 (lag 1, summed across sequences)
as.data.frame(d)
#>   seq_id index state
#> 1      1     1     a
#> 2      1     2     b
#> 3      1     3     a
#> 4      2     1     b
#> 5      2     2     c
